summary: Validated (first patch attempt hit the same malformed-hunk error and was re-issued cleanly; validate --run <run> --submission update38.json → valid=true). Swept the retained changelog for maintainer acknowledgements after the TODO discovery, and recorded two Facts plus a successor interpretation that anchor and reframe the non-voter transfer finding. One release's improvement list states that non-voters were prevented from becoming eligible for leadership elections (CHANGELOG.md:88-98) — exactly the property my finding shows is incomplete, because that protection works on the follower route (the heartbeat-timeout path checks whether the local server has a vote) while the transfer path sets the candidate state directly without consulting suffrage, so a non-voting member can still be pushed into a candidacy by a TimeoutNow: it cannot win, but the incumbent loses leadership and the caller is told the transfer succeeded. The same list records rejecting transfer requests from a candidate state to prevent indefinite blocking, and a later bug-fix list records a race in the transfer-candidacy flag (54-56), so under that history the finding reads as a residual gap of an acknowledged protection rather than a novel mechanism, and the maintainers demonstrably treat transfer-triggered stalls as a defect class. The same release also documents the origin of the escape field behind the shutdown-completion finding — futures were allowed to react to shutdown to prevent a deadlock with snapshotting — which explains why the snapshot-related futures carry it and the user-facing ones do not, placing that remaining gap outside the fix's scope rather than making it a missing mechanism. Counterevidence kept explicit: a changelog entry describes a past change rather than the current contract and is used only as intent evidence; the acknowledged protection may have been deliberately scoped to the election route; the candidate-state rejection is a different case from naming a non-voting target; the shutdown entry does not address the coverage gap (separately acknowledged in a test comment); and nothing was executed.
